doc: Fleet cron as code (#241, parent #160). fleet/cron.py RENDERS the multi-job crontab from this file — never hand-edit the installed crontab lines; `fleet/cron.py install` / `reconcile` is the single writer. The pattern is harvested from kushin77/leaderboard config/fleet-jobs.json (see docs/CANNIBALIZATION.md §12 and docs/MECHANICAL-EXECUTION-LAYER.md §6 — REFERENCE, read for shape only; no source copied).

jobs.name: reap
jobs.why: issue #1360: the rung must pass --branches. The reaper's branch half (landed lane branches, by content — #1118) runs ONLY with that flag, so a rung without it reaps worktrees and lets landed branches pile up until each one ages past check-reconcile's 24h grace and reds the gate of record for every lane. --apply is the half that acts at all: without it the rung reports and reclaims nothing. Both flags are held by name in scripts/check-reap-branches.sh.

jobs.name: promote-portal
jobs.why: declared but not scheduled (issue #1329/#1336): needs the Artifact Registry reader credential the owner places once per docs/AGENTCONSOLE-HOSTING.md §5c (AO_FLEET_AR_READER_KEY_FILE or AO_FLEET_AR_ACCESS_TOKEN_CMD); flipping this to true is that owner's one-line follow-up.

jobs.name: runner
jobs.doc: issue #1343: the shared-services PR runner (docs/PR-RUNNER.md). Role-gated, not flag-gated: installed only where the env contract says AO_RUNNER_HOST_ROLE=primary (the shared-services pair); declared and reconciled everywhere. Since #1506 it is also the SCHEDULED invoker of the verb scripts/gate-status.sh conclude: every cycle publishes the CI venue of record's own concluded verdict for each open PR head that carries no ao/gate-of-record at all (fleet/runner/verify.py, the verdict-convergence pass). The schedule reaches that verb in one hop from this command, which scripts/check-gate-status-scheduled.sh proves by measurement rather than by reading this sentence. The venue's own recipe is not the invoker and cannot be: infra/cloudbuild/verify.yaml posts nothing by design (#1415) and its image carries neither gh nor gcloud (#1350/#1361).
